en: The amihan wind brings cool, dry weather to the Philippines during the first few months of the year.
Clay soil retains water effectively, making it ideal for flooding the paddies of the Banaue Rice Terraces.
Pumice is a lightweight volcanic rock that contains so many gas bubbles it can float on water.
During transpiration, plants release invisible water vapor into the air through tiny pores in their leaves.
Venus appears as the brightest morning star in the sky because its thick clouds reflect sunlight strongly.
Filipino fishermen traditionally use the Talatik constellation, also known as Orion's Belt, to navigate at night.
The moon's gravitational pull causes the ocean water in Manila Bay to rise and fall daily.
A storm surge pushes a massive wall of ocean water onto land during a strong typhoon.
Cumulonimbus clouds grow very tall and produce the heavy rain and thunder during afternoon tropical thunderstorms.
Granite, an igneous rock containing visible black and pink crystals, is commonly used for Philippine monuments.
Water vapor in the warm air condenses into liquid droplets on the outside of a cold glass.
Heavy rains wash loose volcanic ash down the slopes of Mayon Volcano to form destructive mudflows called lahars.
